article.dek: Saturday brought real news: Kansas City loses two cornerbacks before Denver, the Chargers put Derwin James on injured reserve, and New England loses two starters for Miami — while the app's cards hold into Sunday.

items.headline: Lead: Saturday moves — Chiefs down two corners, James to IR, Patriots lose two starters
paragraphs: Kansas City's secondary took two hits Saturday. The Chiefs placed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve and downgraded rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to out with a shoulder injury for Sunday's game at Denver. That is two cover men gone for a division road trip, announced the same afternoon.

The Chargers placed safety Derwin James on injured reserve Saturday after a hamstring setback. James has been out since Week 3, and the move pushes his earliest return to Week 12. The Chargers also ruled out guard Kayode Awosika, defensive back Deane Leonard and receiver Brenen Thompson for Sunday against the Rams, while corners Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley are questionable. Receiver Ladd McConkey is expected to play.

New England lost two starters for Sunday at Miami. Receiver A.J. Brown was ruled out with an ankle injury after missing practice Thursday and Friday, and running back TreVeyon Henderson was ruled out Saturday with an illness.
items.takeaway: Two Chiefs corners are out at Denver, Derwin James is on injured reserve, and the Patriots go to Miami without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Friday's designations stand, plus Monday's Bears-Seahawks report
paragraphs: Friday's clearances still stand: Lamar Jackson is cleared to return for Baltimore at Buffalo, and Saquon Barkley is cleared for Philadelphia at Washington. No new news Saturday changed either one.

The outs from Friday's final reports still stand too: Philadelphia is without DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey and Jonathan Jones. Washington is without starting defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw. Baltimore is without Vega Ioane and Jaylinn Hawkins.

The questionables to carry into Sunday: Buffalo's DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid, Philadelphia's Jakorian Bennett, Washington's Daron Payne, John Bates, Treylon Burks and Jer'Zhan Newton, and Denver's Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Garett Bolles (hip). Denver already ruled out running back RJ Harvey with a knee injury.

Monday night has its own report now. Chicago ruled out running back Kyle Monangai with a toe injury — his fourth straight missed game — and listed cornerback Malik Muhammad and linebacker D'Marco Jackson as questionable. Tight end Colston Loveland was cleared and linebacker T.J. Edwards returns. Seattle ruled out receiver Rashid Shaheed with a knee injury Saturday; running back Zach Charbonnet was removed from the injury report but has not yet been activated from injured reserve.
Questionable does not mean out. The inactive lists about 90 minutes before kickoff are the next real update — check them before you lock anything in on those games.
items.takeaway: Jackson and Barkley are still cleared, the Friday outs and questionables carry into Sunday, and Monday's Bears-Seahawks report adds Monangai out and Shaheed out.

items.headline: Weather: calm and dry across Sunday's outdoor games
paragraphs: Sunday's outdoor games get a calm, dry forecast. In Buffalo, the National Weather Service calls for the lower 60s at the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff against Baltimore, mostly cloudy skies, a gentle south wind and no chance of precipitation through the game.
In Denver, Sunday afternoon looks cloudy with temperatures in the low 60s around the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff against Kansas City, a light north-northeast wind and only a small rain chance.

In Landover for Sunday night, the National Weather Service hourly forecast has about 51 degrees at the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff between Philadelphia and Washington, a near-calm southeast wind, zero percent rain chance, and temperatures falling into the 40s as the game goes on.
That is the forecast as it stands Saturday evening, reported as fact. It is not a reason to bet a total one way or the other.
items.takeaway: Buffalo: lower 60s, no rain. Denver: cloudy, low 60s. Landover: about 51 at kickoff, falling into the 40s, no rain.

items.headline: Evening cards: Hit Rate price improves, Balanced and Value hold
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the Los Angeles Rams moneyline at -265 at DraftKings, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET against the Chargers. It is the pick the app rates most likely to win, with a model probability of 0.649. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. The price improved from -278 this morning, so the same pick costs less than it did at breakfast.
Balanced is Baltimore +3 at -104 at FanDuel, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET at Buffalo. It is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, and a good starting point for a new bettor.
Value is Chicago +3 at -105 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Seattle. Value is always the model's +EV play. The app rates it at a model probability of 0.506 with medium reliability.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate: Rams moneyline -265, down from -278. Balanced: Baltimore +3 -104 at FanDuel. Value: Chicago +3 -105 at DraftKings.

items.headline: A card that holds still means checking your own price
paragraphs: The cards above are priced at DraftKings and FanDuel. If your book is neither, the card price is not your price.

Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the one that matters — run it through Check and let that verdict decide.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: what the moneyline means
paragraphs: The moneyline is the simplest bet in the book: pick the team that wins the game outright. There is no spread to cover, just a winner.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say a team is listed at -150 on the moneyline. The minus sign means that team is favored, and -150 means every $1.50 you risk wins $1. A team listed at +150 is the underdog, and +150 means every $1 you risk wins $1.50.
That is why a heavy moneyline favorite can look safe and still pay very little. You are not betting on how much a team wins by — only that it wins. The price tells you how much that win is worth.
items.takeaway: The moneyline pays on the outright winner only — the minus price is what you risk to win $1, and the plus price is what $1 wins you.

items.headline: Evening board vs morning board: one price improves, no card changes
paragraphs: The evening board makes no card changes. Hit Rate, Balanced and Value are the same three picks as this morning.
The one move: the Rams moneyline improved from -278 to -265 at DraftKings, with the play-through price moving from -283 to -269. Same pick, cheaper than it was this morning.
Everything else on the cards held: Baltimore +3 at -104 at FanDuel and Chicago +3 at -105 at DraftKings are unchanged, play-through prices included. The evening refresh caught all of it.
If your book shows something different from the prices above, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you.
items.takeaway: No card changes — the Rams moneyline improved to -265, and the other two cards are unchanged.

items.headline: Saturday night job: set Sunday up, then wait for one thing only
paragraphs: There is one piece of information worth waiting for: the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before each Sunday kickoff, for the questionable names above. That is a real pending event with a set time.
Everything else is ready now. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet now — waiting for the Sunday rush lets the number drift the wrong way too, especially on big-name teams.

One more habit for the weekend: settlement in the app is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds winners is not a record, it is a highlight reel.
items.takeaway: Wait only for Sunday's inactive lists; otherwise bet when Check says bet — and log every result, winners and losers alike.

article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Evening Brief

evidence.fact: The Kansas City Chiefs placed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve Saturday, Oct. 31, and downgraded rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to out for Sunday's game at Denver with a shoulder injury. Sneed sits at least four games (Denver, Jets, Falcons, Cardinals). Both had been listed questionable. Delane, the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 draft, had an on-and-off shoulder problem for months.

The Los Angeles Chargers placed safety Derwin James on injured reserve Saturday, Oct. 31, after a hamstring setback in his return from the hamstring injury that sidelined him since Week 3; earliest return Week 12 vs New England. The Chargers also ruled out G Kayode Awosika (fibula), DB Deane Leonard (concussion) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) for Sunday vs the Rams; CBs Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley are questionable; WR Ladd McConkey is expected to play after full practices following a Monday concussion absence.

New England Patriots WR A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited Wednesday, downgraded to DNP Thursday and Friday, and ruled out for Week 8 at Miami. Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out Saturday after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday.

Friday's final injury reports still stand Saturday evening: Baltimore QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) carries no game designation and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday Jackson will play Sunday at Buffalo; Philadelphia RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) carries no game designation for Sunday night at Washington. Philadelphia ruled out WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), LB Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), WR Britain Covey (knee) and CB Jonathan Jones (hamstring); CB Jakorian Bennett questionable (knee). Washington ruled out starting DL Javon Kinlaw; DL Daron Payne (foot), TE John Bates, WR Treylon Burks and DL Jer'Zhan Newton questionable. Buffalo listed WR DJ Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid questionable. Baltimore ruled out RG Vega Ioane (knee) and S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee). Denver ruled out RB RJ Harvey (knee); WR Jaylen Waddle (chest) and LT Garett Bolles (hip) questionable.

Chicago Bears final injury report for Monday night vs Seattle, filed Saturday: RB Kyle Monangai (toe) did not practice all week and is ruled out, his fourth straight missed game; CB Malik Muhammad (toe) and LB D'Marco Jackson (ankle) questionable; TE Colston Loveland (neck) removed from the injury report; LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) returns.

Seattle Seahawks WR Rashid Shaheed (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 on Saturday. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday but the team has yet to activate him from injured reserve.

Sunday, Nov. 1 outdoor-game forecasts checked Saturday evening: Buffalo (Ravens at Bills, 1:00 p.m. ET) — National Weather Service Buffalo: lower 60s at kickoff, mostly cloudy, gentle south winds, no precipitation chance through the game. Denver (Chiefs at Broncos, 4:25 p.m. ET) — cloudy, daytime high around 62, light north-northeast wind near 7 mph, rain chance around 20%. Landover (Eagles at Commanders, 8:20 p.m. ET) — National Weather Service hourly: about 51 degrees at 8 p.m., southeast wind around 1 mph, 0% rain chance through the game window, falling into the 40s late.
